episode.title: A word with the last Afghan general

I used to be in the [NDS] back in 2016, 17, and 18, and first one month of 19

persons.name: Sirajuddin Haqqani
persons.role: Haqqani Network leader; wants more power (the prime minister's post, 'caliph') but is limited by Hibatullah; has not gone to his office for three or four months; Alizai says he could one day decapitate Hibatullah or rejoin ISKP as a regional 'khalifa'

events.description: Collapse of the Afghan Republic ('almost four years' before the episode); president, VP, armed forces, judiciary and parliament all escaped.
Khalil Haqqani ('Hakani's uncle', deputy PM) assassinated 'last year'; Haqqanis suspect the Kandahar Taliban, not ISIS; Hibatullah warned Mullah Shirin and Wafa to beware revenge.
'Qari Ahmadullah' killed in the military hospital in the initial days of Taliban rule (one of several intra-Taliban killings).
Balkh governor and other lower-ranking Taliban leaders killed; one or two claimed by ISIS, the rest unattributed.
NDS intelligence 2016-early 2019 showed Haqqanis 'teaming up' with ISKP, passing operations back and forth 'like football'.
A senior Taliban official who publicly complained 'a few months ago' escaped Afghanistan and now lives in Dubai.
Sirajuddin Haqqani has not gone to his office for three or four months; the deputy-PM post left by Khalil's killing remains unfilled.
Amrullah Saleh declared himself president after the collapse.
Amrullah Saleh said he would no longer be president ('last year').
Up to 10,000 Afghans under Temporary Protected Status in the US must begin to self-deport 'in about a month'.
Eid al-Adha 'in four days on Friday' (dates recording to early June 2025); Afghans report lacking food.
State Department's CARE office for Afghan evacuation shut down; Afghanistan has no embassy in the US; embassies closing from India to Europe.
Iran and Pakistan deporting former Afghan soldiers who sought refuge; Taliban jail and torture returnees.
Rumors that the Trump administration will 'give the Taliban a chance' as it did Jolani in Syria; no deal yet.
Taliban spokesmen denied ISIS existed in Afghanistan; today they confirm hunting ISKP.

key_claims: The Taliban are split into Kandahar, Haqqani and Helmand factions that distrust each other over power and resources; Siraj Haqqani wants the premiership and is boycotting his office.
Khalil Haqqani's 2024 assassination is suspected by the Haqqanis to be the Kandahar Taliban's work, and Hibatullah warned his associates of Haqqani revenge.
NDS reporting from 2016-19 showed the Haqqanis operating hand-in-glove with ISKP; Alizai thinks Siraj could rejoin ISKP as a regional khalifa.
ISKP is a bigger threat to the Taliban than the armed resistance (NRF, AFF), which lacks unity, strategy and resources and depends on regional hosts (Tajikistan, Iran, even Pakistan).
The Taliban's only real fear is the US/NATO-trained ANDSF, so they jail, torture and assassinate former soldiers; Iran and Pakistan deporting ex-soldiers feeds this.
Pakistan and Iran maintain deep covert ties with the Taliban despite public hostility; Iranians advise the Taliban on stalling Washington.
A Pashtun-led resistance is needed to strip the Taliban of their 'Pashtun' cover and avoid a 1990s-style civil war.
Ending TPS and closing Afghan embassies/CARE signals to allies that partnering with America is risky.
